title: Single-use approval
description: ADR-001 §5.0 and effects.md §1. An approval binds {transaction digest, exact diff, agent identity, manifest digest, EXACT computed effect set, RFC 8785 canonical operation/body digest, expiry, nonce} — never a singular 'effect class'. Approvals are issued at Gate 2; the schema lands at Gate 0 because the binding it encodes is a Gate 0 exit condition, and because writing it down is what makes the broker's computed binding checkable.

tx_digest.description: Present for D/M transactions; absent for a standalone E step, which has no transaction.

effect_set.description: The exact set computed by the broker pre-execution, not the tool's static minimum. An approval matching a different set is not this approval.

single_use.description: Always true. Consumption is durable and happens BEFORE dispatch — fsync first, send second — so a crash yields DISPATCHING, never a reusable approval (effects.md §3b).

channel.description: The channel that issued the decision. If it is relayed by the same runtime that made the request, approval degrades to friction (threat model).

canonicalOperation.description: The operation as the broker validated and schema-projected it, plus the digest over its canonical bytes. The canonicalization is named on the record so a future change is a visible migration, not a silent reinterpretation of stored approvals.
